newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel 1997 tax revenues up 4.6 pct through April.
newsitem.headline: Israel 1997 tax revenues up 4.6 pct through April.

text.p: The Israeli government's revenues from taxes and fees in the first four months of 1997 totalled 35.3 billion shekels ($10.35 billion), up a real 4.6 percent from a year earlier, the Treasury said on Sunday.
It added however, that discounting changes in tax regulations, there was no increase.

Weak tax revenues, amid an economic slowdown, threaten the government's ability to meet its budget deficit target for fiscal 1997, set at 2.8 percent of gross domestic product. The Treasury is proposing further budget cuts due to the slowdown in tax collection.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu met Finance Minister Dan Meridor on Sunday to discuss possible further cuts in the 1997 budget. The 1997 budget of 197 billion shekels already includes a seven billion shekel cut.
The Israeli government had a deficit of 928 million shekels in the first four months of the year.
Sources in the prime minister's office said new cuts could be presented to the cabinet within two weeks.
